attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: Keeps 'seemingly', 'every software product' and 'wants to add'. 'Seemingly' marks how things look and is rhetorical breadth, not a probability hedge, so this stays a broad observation.

contract.note: Reading 'seemingly every' as a broad market generalisation is fair and ordinary. Counting a stated intended benefit as an explanation is reasonable. The January 2024 window was chosen by the evaluator but is defensible.

evidence.note: Microsoft's Jan 15, 2024 post, quoting a customer, names a concrete benefit (meeting summaries). It is one vendor's own disclosure, and one example cannot contradict a market-wide claim, so it is context, not a contradiction.
Asana's Oct 2023 announcement lists concrete AI features. It falls outside the January window and is a single vendor, so it is context.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires a broad sample of vendors coded for whether they explained benefits. The packet has only two self-descriptions from vendors, one of them before the period, and the drafter admits no representative sample was found. Isolated examples of stated benefits cannot settle how common the practice was, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: The homepage clause is pulled out faithfully from a list of harms. It is a present-tense observation with no hedge.

contract.note: Reading 'full of' as recurring, prominent prevalence is fair. Requiring the content to be AI-generated rather than merely AI-selected is a defensible reading of 'spun', though somewhat strict. The outcome is the same under either reading given this packet.

evidence.note: CNN, Nov 2023: false stories appeared on MSN after editors were replaced by AI curation. It describes selection rather than verified generation, comes before the period, and gives no prevalence measure.

Preprint measuring synthetic articles up to May 2023: the growth was mostly on small sites. It covers a different period and metric and does not measure homepages; at most it cautions against the claim.

reviews.rationale: There is no audit of popular homepages in January 2024. CNN documents incidents on MSN but does not establish that the content was AI-generated or how common it was. The preprint covers a different period and measure. The packet neither supports nor contradicts the claim.
